svg.title: Its support is contained in the compact annulus 1/2 ≤∥q∥≤3. For each fixed derivative order j, the derivatives through order j are bounded by a common constant times the indicator of this annulus, uniformly in a ≥0. To prove the heat-factor part, put y = √a q. Its i-th derivative is ai/2 times the i-th derivative of e−∥y∥2. When ∥y∥≤1, the lower bound ∥q∥≥1/2 implies √a ≤2, so compact derivative bounds suffice. When ∥y∥≥1, use √a ≤2∥y∥and the rapid decay of the Gaussian derivatives. Leibniz’s rule and bounded derivatives of MD give the stated common bound.
